text:
maria: quick heads-up — customer reported intermittent hangs when cancelling streaming requests in our go client. they call req = req.WithContext(ctx) then client.Do(req) and ctx.Done() but the tcp conn sticks around and later requests get ECONNRESET errors. log shows 'http2: stream closed' followed by lots of 'stream 0x12345 returned error'. anyone seen this pattern?
josh: hmm, sounds like context not unwinding the HTTP/2 stream. do they call resp.Body.Close() after cancellation? that usually leaks the conn if not. also what Transport settings are they using? :thinking:
maria: they use the default http.Client with our custom http2 transport that we wire up via golang.org/x/net/http2. no explicit IdleConnTimeout, MaxIdleConnsPerHost left at default. we also see client-side resets when server is under spike.
andrew: two suspects: 1) request context cancel doesn't always close underlying stream immediately due to http2 flow control + server not noticing; 2) Conn reuse + idle timer interactions causing stray frames on reused conn. have logs?
maria: pasted minimal snippet and logs below.
maria: ```go
// simplified
tr := &http.Transport{ /* TLS stuff */ }
// http2.ConfigureTransport(tr) done elsewhere
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
req, _ := http.NewRequest("GET", url, nil)
req = req.WithContext(ctx)
resp, err := client.Do(req)
if err != nil { return err }
// if ctx cancelled we still sometimes see no error and resp.Body is nil
```
maria: log excerpt: 
```
2026-02-12T10:23:01Z caller=client.go:142 msg="request start" id=abc
2026-02-12T10:23:02Z caller=client.go:167 msg="ctx cancelled" id=abc
2026-02-12T10:23:02Z net/http: http2: stream closed id=abc
2026-02-12T10:23:05Z net/http: http2: transport: readFrame failure: read tcp 10.0.0.5:443->10.0.0.9:52344: read: connection reset by peer
```
sam: sounds familiar — we had a bug where we didn't set IdleConnTimeout and the connection stayed open longer than the server expected; when server GC'd the stream it sent RST while we thought conn was healthy. setting tr.IdleConnTimeout = 90*time.Second fixed it in one customer case. also set MaxIdleConnsPerHost to >100 if you do high concurrency.
josh: also check ResponseHeaderTimeout and ExpectContinueTimeout. for streaming, ResponseHeaderTimeout shouldn't be too tight. another trick: enable http2's Ping (keepalive) at connection layer if server supports it so you detect dead peers earlier.
andrew: for context propagation specifically, ensure you use req.WithContext before client.Do. also call resp.Body.Close in a defer even if err != nil — there are some cases where resp is non-nil and has partial streams. if you want aggressive cancel, consider using Transport.CancelRequest equivalent by using a custom RoundTripper that closes underlying conn on cancel. we had an internal small helper that wraps RoundTripper and calls CloseIdleConnections for that host on cancel.
maria: nice. i can try adding explicit resp.Body.Close and set IdleConnTimeout. question: do we want to change SDK defaults or just doc this?
sam: we should change SDK defaults IMO. set IdleConnTimeout to 60s, MaxIdleConnsPerHost to 200, and add a small wrapper that ensures cancel closes the conn for streaming endpoints. we can gate that behind a env flag.
josh: +1 for safer defaults. also add a note in docs about not relying solely on context cancellation to tear down http2 streams.
maria: i'll prototype a wrapper. quick prototype idea: on ctx.Done() call transport.CloseIdleConnections() scoped to the single net.Conn — tricky but workable with a conn tracker. otherwise CloseIdleConnections is coarse.
andrew: we also should create a minimal repro for QA — simple server that delays ACK and client cancels after x ms. file an eng-runtime issue and cc eng-platform for tuning advice.
maria: filing issue now, will attach repro and logs. tagging @josh @sam for review. :eyes:
deploy-bot: issue #INFR-1187 created by maria: "go client http2 streaming cancel leads to conn reuse resets" assigned to eng-runtime.
maria: (action) add test + config PR by EOD tomorrow, i'll include both docs and code change.
sam: if you need help with conn-tracker i can pair.
josh: when you open the PR, include benchmark showing no regression in P95 latency for non-cancel flows. :shipit:
maria: thanks all — i'll update thread with repro link and PR soon.
